title: How Modern Monetary Theory Can Bridge The Gap Between Left-and Right-wing Populism

detail.title: How Modern Monetary Theory Can Bridge The Gap Between Left-and Right-wing Populism
detail.abstract:
This paper traces the evolution of American populism from its agrarian roots in the 1890s through its twenty-first-century transformations across the ideological spectrum. It argues that populism, rather than a fixed ideology, is a recurring democratic impulse arising from cycles of economic dislocation, political exclusion, and cultural alienation. The study identifies four major historical phases: the agrarian and Progressive populisms of the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries; the cultural realignment of the postwar and Cold War eras; the neoliberal globalization of the 1980s–2000s and its discontents; and the rise of left- and right-wing populisms since the 2010s.

In recent years, five major movements—Democratic Socialists, Progressive Democrats, America First, American Compass, and MAGA — have emerged. They are analyzed comparatively across economic, societal, and institutional dimensions. Despite sharp moral and political differences, these groups share a skepticism of globalization, a preference for production over consumption, and a belief that elites have betrayed the national interest.
The paper then introduces Modern Monetary Theory (MMT) as both a descriptive and proscriptive framework for understanding sovereign fiscal capacity and its implications for populist policy. Drawing on the work of MMT economists, it shows how MMT reframes government spending, taxation, and employment policy around real-resource limits rather than financial constraints. MMT thus provides a conceptual bridge between left- and right-populist objectives—linking calls for economic justice, industrial renewal, and national resilience under a shared recognition of fiscal sovereignty.
The conclusion contends that populism’s endurance reflects a deeper crisis of democratic legitimacy: citizens’ loss of faith that government represents their interests. Yet by clarifying the true nature of fiscal capacity, MMT offers a path from grievance to governance, enabling a post-neoliberal politics centered on full employment, public investment, and renewed democratic purpose.

AI.theoretical_framework: 民粹主义理论、现代货币理论(MMT)、民主合法性理论
AI.method: 历史分析、比较分析、理论框架应用
AI.findings: 识别了民粹主义的四个历史阶段；当代五个主要民粹运动虽然存在道德和政治差异，但都对全球化持怀疑态度，偏好生产而非消费，认为精英背叛了国家利益；MMT为左右翼民粹目标提供了概念桥梁。

title: Training and Entrepreneurship: Evidence from Ghana
affiliations: Johns Hopkins University - Paul H. Nitze School of Advanced International Studies (SAIS), Wellesley College and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Training and Entrepreneurship: Evidence from Ghana
detail.abstract: Entrepreneurship is seen as a key driver of economic growth, which has led to an increased interest in policy interventions such as business incubators. These incubators comprise various components including funding and training. We conduct a randomized controlled trial to determine the causal effect of the training component of incubators on entrepreneurship. We design and deliver a training program to undergraduate business school students in Ghana interested in starting a business. We will evaluate the effects of this training program on soft skills, business knowledge, the likelihood of business creation, and the subsequent performance of the business. We will also analyze potential spillovers to peers in the control group. Our findings will contribute to our understanding of which components of business incubators effectively promote entrepreneurship, and the extent to which these programs can generate broader impacts beyond the direct participants.

title: Privacy-Preserving Transparency: A ZKP Framework for Mortgage Lending in Emerging Economies
affiliations: University of South Carolina

detail.title: Privacy-Preserving Transparency: A ZKP Framework for Mortgage Lending in Emerging Economies
detail.abstract: Persistent opacity in property and income reporting constrains mortgage lending and financial inclusion across emerging economies. In India, under-valuation of property and unverifiable borrower data inflate risk premiums and restrict access to formal credit. This paper develops a Zero-Knowledge Proof (ZKP)-based mortgage verification framework that enables lenders to validate loan-to-value, debt-to-income, and KYC compliance without accessing sensitive financial or ownership information. The proposed system integrates economic modeling, cryptographic design, and implementation feasibility within India's digital public infrastructure. Simulation results calibrated to 2019-2024 data show that reductions in opacity substantially lower effective interest spreads, expand credit volumes, and generate sustained welfare gains through improved capital allocation. The phased rollout architecture demonstrates how ZKPs can evolve from a technical innovation to a public-good infrastructure layer for transparent yet privacy-preserving credit markets. The study contributes to the literature on digital financial inclusion, showing how cryptographic verification can complement institutional reform in advancing trust, efficiency, and market depth.

title: Governance in a Hard-Edged World: ESG, the JSE, and Africa’s Capital Advantage

detail.title: Governance in a Hard-Edged World: ESG, the JSE, and Africa’s Capital Advantage

declarations.declarationOfInterest: No Declaration
declarations.funderStatement: Not Applicable

detail.abstract:
War-time supply chains, energy shocks, and information risk have turned Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) from rhetoric into operating reality. In Africa, leadership is now judged by how effectively firms secure energy, protect people, govern technology, and disclose decision-useful data. This paper outlines why Risk Insights (RI) built ESG GPS™, Africa’s first AI-driven ESG data infrastructure, translating global standards into local realities across nine African stock exchanges and extending into the Gulf and North Africa.

Through partnerships with exchanges such as the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE), RI has advanced data comparability, disclosure quality, and investor confidence, critical enablers of market depth and fairer capital allocation. The paper also analyses South Africa’s self-regulatory exchange model and the governance, competitiveness, and trust implications in a multipolar world.

The argument is clear: Africa’s opportunity lies in credible, data-driven ESG ecosystems that enable stakeholder value, not agency theory, as the foundation for resilient markets and sustainable growth.

AI.tldr: 本文介绍了Risk Insights开发的ESG GPS™，这是非洲首个AI驱动的ESG数据基础设施，将全球标准转化为非洲九个证券交易所的本地现实，并扩展到海湾和北非地区。通过与约翰内斯堡证券交易所等合作，提高了数据可比性、披露质量和投资者信心，这对市场深度和更公平的资本配置至关重要。

AI.motivation: 战时供应链、能源冲击和信息风险使ESG从修辞转变为运营现实，非洲领导力现在通过企业如何有效保障能源、保护人员、治理技术和披露有用数据来评判。
AI.theoretical_framework: 以利益相关者价值而非代理理论为基础，强调可信的ESG生态系统对市场韧性的重要性。
AI.method: 通过与证券交易所合作建立AI驱动的ESG数据基础设施，分析南非的自律性交易所模式。
AI.findings: ESG GPS™提高了数据可比性、披露质量和投资者信心，是市场深度和公平资本配置的关键推动因素。
AI.theory_contributions: 提出了以利益相关者价值而非代理理论为基础的ESG生态系统理论框架，强调数据驱动方法对市场韧性的重要性。
AI.practical_contributions: 开发了非洲首个AI驱动的ESG数据基础设施，与九个非洲证券交易所合作，提高了ESG数据的可用性和质量，促进了更公平的资本配置。

title: JUE Insight: The Cost of Crime: Evidence from Short-Term Rentals
affiliations: University of Connecticut, University of Connecticut - Department of Agricultural and Resource Economics and the National Center for Smart Growth and University of Connecticut

detail.title: JUE Insight: The Cost of Crime: Evidence from Short-Term Rentals
detail.abstract: Using transaction-level short-term rental (STR) data from New York City, we link daily booking prices to recent street-level violent crime to quantify local economic costs andinfer the Value of Statistical Life (VSL). One additional violent crime within 500 feet produces an annualized neighborhood revenue loss of $351. Mapping the same risk–price tradeoff to mortality risk yields a VSL of $4.3 million (2020 USD), with estimate range from $2.8–$9.4 million across alternative specifications. Our rich, high-frequency data provides a novel setting to estimate risk-price tradeoffs in perceived public safety.

title: Predicting Length of Productive Lifespan and Lifetime Production in Swiss Dairy Cows from Herd Book Data of First Versus Second Lactation
affiliations: Research Institute of Organic Agriculture (FiBL), University of Kassel, Research Institute of Organic Agriculture (FiBL), Research Institute of Organic Agriculture (FiBL), university of padova, university of padova and Research Institute of Organic Agriculture (FiBL)

detail.title: Predicting Length of Productive Lifespan and Lifetime Production in Swiss Dairy Cows from Herd Book Data of First Versus Second Lactation
detail.abstract: Dairy cows’ longevity is a crucial trait integrating multiple functional traits and impacting sustainability of dairy production. This study evaluated the impact of productive lifespan on lifetime productivity in Swiss low-input dairy systems, compared the predictability of longevity and lifetime production using first- versus second-lactation data, and tested whether lactation curve parameters (LCP) based on test-day records improve predictions. Herd book data of culled Swiss dairy cows from low-input and organic farms were used to predict (1) length of productive lifespan (LPL, days from first calving to culling) and (2) the number of lactations (MaxLN) applying generalized linear mixed models. Additionally, lifetime milk production (LTP_ECM) and daily milk yield during length of productive lifespan (DMY_LPL_ECM) were studied. Records from first and second lactation were used in three datasets: (a) large (n= 10,031 cows, 384 farms), (b) reduced data set with insemination records (n= 6,011 cows, 372 farms), and (c) small data set with LCP (n=1,632 cows, 321 farms). Models based on second-lactation data consistently outperformed those using first-lactation data. The best models for LPL, MaxLN, and LTP_ECM were from datasets with complete insemination records, although predictability remained low (5.0%, 6.0%, and 11.7%, respectively). Models including LCP performed best for DMY_LPL_ECM with mean predictability of 73.5%. Predictive accuracy improved with additional factors such as somatic cell count, breed, calving interval, age at first calving, lactation curve persistency, milk yield traits, fat-protein ratio, and alpine pasturing. While lifetime production traits can be reasonably predicted with farm-available data, predicting longevity remains difficult.

AI.tldr: 本研究评估了瑞士低投入奶牛系统中生产寿命对终身生产力的影响，比较了使用第一泌乳期与第二泌乳期数据预测寿命和终身生产的能力，并测试了基于测试日记录的泌乳曲线参数是否能改善预测效果。
AI.research_question: 1) 生产寿命如何影响奶牛终身生产力？2) 使用第一泌乳期还是第二泌乳期数据能更好预测寿命和终身生产？3) 泌乳曲线参数是否能改善预测准确性？
AI.motivation: 奶牛寿命是整合多个功能性状并影响乳业可持续性的关键特征，需要了解在低投入系统中如何预测寿命和生产力。
AI.theoretical_framework: 基于奶牛生产性能、泌乳曲线理论和寿命预测模型，研究不同数据源对预测准确性的影响。
AI.method: 使用瑞士低投入和有机农场的淘汰奶牛群记录数据，应用广义线性混合模型预测生产寿命长度、泌乳期数、终身产奶量和日平均产奶量。使用三个数据集：大型数据集、含配种记录的缩减数据集、含泌乳曲线参数的小型数据集。
AI.findings: 基于第二泌乳期数据的模型表现优于第一泌乳期；含完整配种记录的模型对寿命预测效果最好但预测力仍低（5.0%-11.7%）；含泌乳曲线参数的模型对日平均产奶量预测效果最佳（73.5%）；体细胞计数、品种、产犊间隔等因素能改善预测准确性。
AI.theory_contributions: 证实了第二泌乳期数据在预测奶牛寿命和生产力方面的优越性，建立了泌乳曲线参数在生产力预测中的重要价值。
AI.practical_contributions: 为低投入奶牛系统提供了实用的寿命和生产力预测方法，帮助农场主基于可获取数据做出管理决策，虽然寿命预测仍具挑战性但生产力预测相对可靠。

title: The Institutional Evolution Paradox: Democracy, Authoritarianism, and Technological Complexity

detail.title: The Institutional Evolution Paradox: Democracy, Authoritarianism, and Technological Complexity
detail.abstract:
Why do advanced democracies increasingly face stagnation, while certain
authoritarian regimes show unexpected resilience? Traditional theories of
political economy, from modernization theory to the “end of history” thesis,
assumed democracy as the ultimate institutional form. Yet contemporary patterns
— Japan’s long stagnation, Southern Europe’s malaise, contrasted with China’s
and Singapore’s resilience — challenge this view.
Existing research highlights democratic short-termism (Downs, 1957; Acemoglu
& Robinson, 2012), authoritarian adaptation (Nathan, 2003), demographic
headwinds (Bloom, Canning, & Fink, 2010; Horioka & Terada-Hagiwara, 2012),
and the role of AI and big data in governance (Meagher, 2021). However, these
insights remain fragmented. We lack a unified framework explaining why
democracy appears well-suited in earlier development stages but maladaptive in
high-complexity, low-growth environments, while authoritarian regimes,
historically fragile, may now benefit from technological rescue.
This paper proposes the Institutional Evolution Paradox: institutional optimality is
not universal but stage dependent. Democracy fosters innovation and openness
in early development, but electoral short-termism and demographic pressures
create “stable stagnation” in maturity. Conversely, authoritarian regimes
historically failed due to information asymmetry, but AI and big data mitigate
these weaknesses, enabling long-term coordination.
The paradox implies that democracy is not the final endpoint of institutional
evolution but a stage-specific regime type. In the high-complexity era,
authoritarianism may regain viability, leading to a “mixed institutional order” in the
global system. (This is a preliminary version. An empirical section will be added
in subsequent drafts.

AI.tldr: 本文提出了"制度演化悖论"：制度最优性不是普遍的，而是阶段依赖的。民主在早期发展阶段促进创新和开放，但在成熟期因选举短期主义和人口压力导致"稳定停滞"；而威权体制历史上因信息不对称而失败，但AI和大数据缓解了这些弱点，实现了长期协调。
AI.research_question: 为什么发达民主国家日益面临停滞，而某些威权政权却显示出意外的韧性？
AI.motivation: 传统政治经济理论假设民主是最终制度形式，但当代模式（日本长期停滞、南欧困境，与中国和新加坡的韧性形成对比）挑战了这一观点。现有研究见解分散，缺乏统一框架。
AI.theoretical_framework: 制度演化悖论、民主短期主义理论、威权适应理论、人口压力理论、AI和大数据治理理论
AI.method: 理论分析框架构建（论文提到后续草案将添加实证部分）

title: Traceability for Privacy: A Foundational Pillar for an Effective and Competitive EU Digital Rulebook

detail.title: Traceability for Privacy: A Foundational Pillar for an Effective and Competitive EU Digital Rulebook
detail.abstract: The European Union has established a comprehensive digital rulebook (GDPR, DSA, DMA, DGA, Data Act, AI Act), to develop a digital single market that respects fundamental rights. An investigation into this legal framework, however, reveals significant barriers to its effectiveness, including inconsistent enforcement, "gold-plating," and a burdensome compliance landscape for SMEs. This paper's analysis establishes that a standardized, interoperable, and privacy-preserving traceability layer is a critical infrastructural prerequisite to bridge the gap between legal principles and technical enforceability. Traceability, defined as the ability to document the data lifecycle and link processing to a verifiable legal basis, provides the necessary foundation for accountability, a gap in the institutional enforcement system. This paper conducts a legal-technical analysis, first establishing through a systematic review that traceability is a foundational requirement across the EU digital rulebook. Second, it compares technical architectures based on blockchains, attestations (OTrace) and cryptographic claims (W3C Verifiable Credentials). The analysis concludes that while public blockchains present GDPR compliance paradoxes and require workarounds, a careful merger of OTrace and VCs, and an operational framework synthesizing the EU Digital Identity Wallet and Data Governance Act data intermediaries offers a pragmatic, legally-aligned solution to the current institutional deficit. Finally, it connects this "EU-Trace" model to the EuroStack's strategic vision, concluding that a risk-based mandate for traceability can mitigate the negative effects of regulatory fragmentation by harmonizing the mechanism of compliance, thereby enhancing competitiveness for a transparent, accountable digital Europe.

AI.tldr: 本文分析欧盟数字规则手册（GDPR、DSA、DMA等）实施障碍，提出标准化、可互操作且保护隐私的可追溯性层作为关键基础设施，通过结合OTrace和可验证凭证技术，构建"EU-Trace"模型来解决法律原则与技术可执行性之间的差距。
AI.research_question: 欧盟数字规则手册实施面临哪些障碍？如何通过技术解决方案来弥合法律原则与技术可执行性之间的差距？
AI.motivation: 欧盟建立了全面的数字规则手册，但在实施过程中面临执法不一致、"镀金"现象以及中小企业合规负担等障碍，需要找到有效的方法来确保法律原则能够在技术上得到执行。
AI.theoretical_framework: 基于可追溯性理论、问责制理论和数字治理理论，将可追溯性定义为记录数据生命周期并将处理与可验证法律依据相连接的能力。
AI.method: 采用法律-技术分析方法：首先通过系统综述确立可追溯性在欧盟数字规则手册中的基础地位，然后比较基于区块链、证明（OTrace）和加密声明（W3C可验证凭证）的技术架构。
AI.findings: 公共区块链存在GDPR合规悖论，需要变通方案；OTrace与可验证凭证的谨慎结合，结合欧盟数字身份钱包和数据治理法案数据中介的操作框架，提供了符合法律规定的实用解决方案。
AI.theory_contributions: 建立了可追溯性作为数字治理关键基础设施的理论框架，提出了"EU-Trace"模型，为数字规则的技术执行提供了理论支撑。
AI.practical_contributions: 提出了基于风险的强制性可追溯性要求，通过统一合规机制减轻监管碎片化的负面影响，为透明、负责任的数字欧洲增强竞争力。

title: The Logic of Money: Reconstructing the Endogeneity of Money under Institutional Constraints
affiliations: Independent researcher

detail.title: The Logic of Money: Reconstructing the Endogeneity of Money under Institutional Constraints
detail.abstract: Traditional monetary theories, with their aggregate perspectives, fail to explain the structural imbalances and the non-linear relationship between monetary value and aggregate quantity in modern economies. This paper proposes "The Logic of Money: Reconstructing the Endogeneity of Money under Institutional Constraints," which employs a structural analytical framework to redefine the mechanisms of money creation and value anchoring. Building on the prior finding of market under-consumption and structural deficiencies (Huang, 2025a), this study further argues that such deficiencies originate from the inherent imbalance in monetary flow. It introduces a binary framework of structural monetary flows: the Consumption Money Flow (MC) and the Developmental Money Flow (MD). The paper demonstrates that the value of money (VM) is not determined by its aggregate quantity, but is anchored to the structural ratio between productive assets (A) and MC, expressed as the fundamental relation VM ∝ A/MC. On this basis, fiscal deficits (D) are redefined as an institutionally anchored mechanism for endogenous money creation, functioning through deficit-based welfare provision and deficiency rescue to dynamically supplement the MC gap, thereby sustaining the healthy growth of A. This framework shifts macroeconomic policy from a focus on deficit magnitude to one on deficit purpose and institutional efficiency, providing a new theoretical foundation and quantitative path for achieving structural equilibrium and inclusive growth.

AI.tldr: 本文提出结构性货币流动分析框架，将货币流动分为消费性货币流动(MC)和发展性货币流动(MD)，证明货币价值(VM)与生产性资产(A)和MC的结构比率相关(VM ∝ A/MC)，并将财政赤字重新定义为制度锚定的内生货币创造机制。
AI.research_question: 如何从结构性视角重新解释货币创造机制和价值锚定，以及财政赤字在维持结构性均衡中的作用？
AI.motivation: 传统货币理论无法解释现代经济中的结构性失衡和货币价值与总量之间的非线性关系，需要新的分析框架。
AI.theoretical_framework: 结构性货币流动二元框架(MC和MD)、货币价值锚定理论(VM ∝ A/MC)、财政赤字作为内生货币创造机制的理论。
AI.method: 结构性分析框架，基于先前发现的市场经济不足和结构性缺陷，构建理论模型。
AI.findings: 货币价值由生产性资产与消费性货币流动的结构比率决定，财政赤字通过制度锚定机制动态补充MC缺口，维持A的健康增长。
AI.theory_contributions: 重构了货币内生性理论，提出了结构性货币流动分析框架，重新定义了财政赤字的经济功能。
AI.practical_contributions: 为宏观经济政策提供了新理论基础，将政策焦点从赤字规模转向赤字用途和制度效率，为实现结构性均衡和包容性增长提供量化路径。

title: The Price of Progress: Capitalism, Inequality, and the Roots of Global Poverty

detail.title: The Price of Progress: Capitalism, Inequality, and the Roots of Global Poverty

declarations.declarationOfInterest: I, The authors declare that this research, "The Price of Progress: Capitalism, Inequality, and the Roots of Global Poverty," received no specific grant from any public, commercial, or non-profit funding agency and was conducted without any known financial or biasing influence. The work represents an independent, critical, and comparative analysis of economic systems , and the conclusions presented—which move beyond the conventional narrative to identify the structural roots of poverty —were reached after a comprehensive and challenging evaluation of scholarly literature. The authors assert that these findings, including the advocacy for democratic public planning and a new social compact where human welfare, not profit, is the explicit purpose, are the result of rigorous intellectual effort and are not subject to any undisclosed external or internal bias

detail.abstract: This paper deconstructs the conventional narrative that credits capitalism as the primary force for poverty alleviation and human progress. Through a sociological and comparative analysis, it argues that capitalism is not an external solution to poverty, but a complex and contradictory system that intrinsically generates and perpetuates inequality and precarity. Drawing on historical and contemporary scholarship, the study first critiques the empirical foundations of the celebratory narrative, demonstrating how a truncated historical timeline and flawed metrics obscure the dispossessing and de-industrializing effects that accompanied the system's global expansion. The analysis then explores the structural mechanisms inherent to capitalism-including market dependence, the process of primitive accumulation, and the creation of a surplus labor populationthat inevitably produce and reinforce social stratification and insecurity. The paper extends this critique to a comparative moral accounting, juxtaposing the acute casualties of communist regimes with the less-visible but widespread deaths resulting from systemic issues such as chattel slavery, deaths of despair, and environmental degradation under capitalism. Ultimately, the study concludes that a reliance on reactive, market-based solutions is insufficient. It advocates for a fundamental reevaluation of the relationship between economy and society, proposing a new social compact that utilizes proactive state intervention and democratic public planning to address the structural roots of poverty, thereby working toward an economic model where human welfare, not profit, is the explicit purpose.

AI.tldr: 本文解构了传统认为资本主义是减贫和人类进步主要动力的叙事，指出资本主义本身就是一个产生和维持不平等的复杂矛盾系统，主张通过国家干预和民主规划建立以人类福祉为目标的新经济模式。

AI.method: 社会学和比较分析，结合历史和当代学术研究，进行批判性分析和道德比较。
AI.findings: 资本主义不是贫困的外部解决方案，而是内在产生不平等的系统；传统叙事基于被截断的时间线和有缺陷的指标；资本主义的结构机制必然产生社会分层和不安全感。

title: Ombudsman Institutions: A Study in the Light of Shariah and Pakistani Law

keywords: Shariah Guidelines Regarding Office of Muhtasib
Differences Between Accountability Mechanisms of Earlier Islamic States and Pakistan

detail.abstract: Before a few centuries, the word "Ombudsman" was begun to be used as a public office which redressed the public grievances and held public officials accountable for their injustices and abuse of power. But, the concept and philosophy behind this very institution is as old as the concept of public office. Existing literature shows that civilized societies have developed this concept to ensure check and balance above the ruling class. Islam, being a gap-less system, always preferred accountability of public officials in order to watch the ruling class, constituting it as an essential manifesto of the Islamic State. It is based on the Islamic politico-legal Philosophy and includes Shariah doctrines of "Adl" (Justice) and "hisbah" and the one who exercises this function of accountability is commonly known as "Muhtasib". Concerning it, this study seeks to explore the history and philosophy of Ombudsman institutions and its concept. Central to it, this study is dedicated to analyze the concept of Ombudsman or Muhtasib in the light of Shariah and Pakistani Law. It will also highlight the famous doctrine of Islamic Law like "Hisbah" and draw a sketch of Office of Muhtasib from the era of Khulfa-e-Rashiddin and explain how this institution was working in earlier Islamic State. This article will also explore the legal frameworks regarding Ombudsman Institutions in Pakistan and their compatibility with the office of Muhtasib in earlier Islamic States. The article will also identify the loop holes in Pakistani Ombudsman Institutions on the basis of traditional Hisbah Institutions and suggest certain recommendations for its improvement.

detail.abstract: In early 2010, Greece's financial condition was unsustainable, necessitating the implementation of ambitious economic adjustment programs. The fiscal austerity measures launched by the Greek government in agreement with its official creditors (IMF, ECB and European member states) led to a rather deep recession as GDP dropped by 25% and unemployment peaked at 25%. Households' income, corporations' profit, as well as their debt-paying ability decreased significantly leading to a huge amount of non-performing loans (NPLs). This paper provides a complete analysis of the measures introduced by the Greek government to stabilize Greek banks and reduce NPLs ratio at single digits.

title: Shifting Financial Hierarchies: China's Financial Statecraft Overseas in ASEAN and Latin America

detail.title: Shifting Financial Hierarchies: China's Financial Statecraft Overseas in ASEAN and Latin America
detail.abstract: The United States and European Union have increasingly abandoned neoliberal orthodoxy in favour of protectionist industrial policies and state intervention, weaponizing economic tools for geopolitical objectives rather than market efficiency. Concurrently, the hegemony of the U.S. dollar faces erosion through bilateral trade shifts, currency swap arrangements, and technological innovations including cryptocurrencies and alternative payment systems. While the dollar's dominance persists-maintaining 50-60% shares across key monetary functions compared to the RMB's sub-5%-incremental transformations are evident in China's construction of financial infrastructures that bypass SWIFT and reduce USD dependencies. We contend that U.S. policy inconsistencies reflect a strategic pivot: economic and financial considerations have become subordinate to securing long-term dominance in the technological order, where first-mover advantages determine decades of hegemonic power. This explains ostensibly erratic behaviours, from pressuring the Federal Reserve on interest rates to compelling European bond purchases. Through case studies of China's financial engagement with ASEAN and Latin America, we demonstrate how distinct pathways toward de-dollarization are emerging-one characterized by proximate, trade-intensive integration fostering organic RMB adoption through fintech synergies, the other by distant, resource-driven diversification capitalizing on historical resentment of U.S. influence. These regional infrastructures provide the Global South with enhanced monetary autonomy, cheaper payment alternatives, and crisis mitigation tools. While China cannot displace the USD-cantered order imminently, it is systematically constructing parallel architectures that incrementally challenge dollar hegemony, redefining international finance through technological and institutional innovation rather than direct confrontation.

detail.abstract: AI technology has significant and profound applications in the financial sector, with its value increasingly evident in critical areas such as credit approval, anti-fraud measures, and intelligent customer service. However, the effective implementation of AI is not only constrained by technical factors but is also frequently hindered by organizational structures and trust-related issues. Current research predominantly focuses on the pre-adoption phase of AI technology, neglecting the dynamic mechanisms for organizational integration and strategic transformation post-adoption. detail.title: Distributional Energy Justice and the Inclusive Human Development Agenda in Africa

detail.abstract: This study advances the economic development scholarship through three key contributions. First, it examines the impact of distributional energy justice (hereafter, energy justice) on inclusive human development (IHDI) in Africa. Second, we investigate how climate readiness moderates the effect of energy justice on IHDI. Third, we explore whether the joint effect of energy justice and climate readiness differs across low-and high-income African countries. We make these contributions using macro data for 36 African countries from 2010 to 2020. The results reveal that energy justice promotes IHDI. The contingency analysis also demonstrates that climate readiness amplifies the positive impact of energy justice on IHDI. Notably, across the economic, social, and governance perspectives of climate readiness, the results show that the moderating effect of governance readiness is striking. Evidence from sensitivity analysis also suggests that relative to their low-income counterparts, high-income countries realise a remarkable increase in IHDI with progress in energy justice and climate readiness. These findings underscore the urgent need for investments in distributionl energy justice and climate resilience to foster inclusive human development in Africa.

detail.abstract:
Geopolitical Mining argues that minerals are no longer generic commodities—they are instruments of state power—and that leverage in this game sits midstream (conversion, separation, QA/QC, and standards), not in ore alone. We frame a reproducible contrast: China as an engineers’ state that prioritizes build tempo, integration, and delivery; and the United States and allied rule-of-law economies as lawyerly systems that prioritize ex-ante legitimacy through procedural review and enforceable rights. Each logic reliably produces strengths and failure modes across permitting, midstream build-out, and recycling.

We derive a hybrid playbook that preserves voice and remedy while restoring clock certainty: (i) parallel reviews with firm endpoints and on-spec acceptance tests; (ii) bundled, corridor-level infrastructure decisions; (iii) dedicated FOAK lanes with enhanced monitoring; and (iv) blended finance gated by utilization and quality KPIs. Sector lenses—lithium, copper, rare earths—illustrate how tempo × chemistry × legitimacy determines who captures the marginal processed tonne and, ultimately, geopolitical advantage. 

Appendices include a permitting-clock template and a board-level checklist to translate policy into delivery and delivery into durable legitimacy.

detail.abstract: The increasing autonomy of artificial intelligence (AI) systems necessitates a paradigm shift from reactive regulatory compliance to proactive, architecturally enforced ethical governance. Current accountability models struggle to address the opacity of AI decision-making, creating a critical gap in verifiable trust. This paper introduces Ternary Moral Logic (TML), a novel computational ethics architecture designed to bridge immutable technical systems with enforceable moral reasoning. TML operates on a triadic framework that moves beyond binary right/wrong evaluations to a more nuanced, contextaware logic. We detail its Eight Pillars-Sacred Zero and Pause, Always Memory, the Goukassian Promise, Moral Trace Logs, Human Rights, Earth Protection, the Hybrid Shield, and Public Blockchains-which collectively create a system for traceable, verifiable, and auditable accountability in AI operations. By integrating cryptographically sealed logs with ethical directives, TML provides a robust mechanism for ensuring that an AI's actions are not only recorded but are also aligned with predefined moral constraints. We demonstrate TML's practical interoperability with leading international standards, including the EU AI Act, the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, and the IEEE 7000-series, illustrating how it addresses their conceptual gaps by providing an implementable technical backbone for ethical principles. This work concludes that architecturally enforced morality, as embodied by TML, represents the next frontier in AI governance, enabling a future where ethical accountability is a computational reality, not merely a regulatory aspiration.

detail.abstract: This study investigates questionable green ICT practices among major technology companies, revealing significant discrepancies between corporate sustainability claims and actual environmental practices. Using a case study approach supported by a review of media and third-party reports, the research identifies key issues such as greenwashing, inadequate e-waste management, and the questionable effectiveness of carbon offsets. The findings highlight that despite companies like Amazon, Google, Apple, and Microsoft promoting robust green initiatives, their practices often fall short of genuine sustainability, with concerns including misleading claims about energy sources, insufficient lifecycle assessments, and ineffective recycling programs. The study emphasises the need for improved transparency, better e-waste management practices, stricter regulatory oversight, and a critical examination of carbon offset practices. These findings align with UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) 12 and 13, which advocate for sustainable consumption, production, and urgent action to combat climate change, urging corporations to adopt transparent and accountable sustainability practices that contribute to environmental preservation and climate resilience. Achieving progress in ICT sustainability will require not only credible environmental claims but also actionable strategies that deliver tangible outcomes for a sustainable future.

title: Deepfakes for Good: Empirical Analysis and AI Agentic Framework for Bias Measurement and Mitigation
affiliations: University of Maryland - Robert H. Smith School of Business, University of Maryland - Robert H. Smith School of Business and University of Maryland - Robert H. Smith School of Business

detail.title: Deepfakes for Good: Empirical Analysis and AI Agentic Framework for Bias Measurement and Mitigation
detail.abstract: Measuring bias in decision-making remains a significant methodological challenge, as traditional approaches struggle to achieve comparability in sensory data, isolating bias-sensitive elements while maintaining identical conditions across all other factors. This study explores how deepfake technology can be used to address this comparability challenge. Since existing studies lack a clear framework for understanding deepfakes, this study begins with developing a theoretical framework: calibration deepfakes-based on a systematic analysis of 826 academic papers. Our framework enables bias measurement by precisely modifying bias-sensitive elements (e.g., perceived race or age) in sensory data (e.g., visual, audio) while preserving all decision-relevant elements. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this framework through pain assessment experiments with 3,802 assessors evaluating original or deepfake counterparts, revealing systematic biases related to race and age. Notably, such biases manifest in distinct facial regions: White assessors focus primarily on upper facial regions, while Black assessors attend more to lower facial areas. These findings suggest that differential perceptual experience with own-race versus other-race faces drives bias in pain assessments, aligning with perceptual experience theory. Given that human biases are persistent and mitigating them is costly and time-consuming, we further develop a Multi-Agent Debiasing System (MADS) that integrates calibration deepfakes as an alternative, outperforming human assessors in time efficiency, cost-effectiveness, and bias levels. Our work establishes a novel framework for bias measurement, repurposing controversial technologies for societal benefit, and provides actionable insights for bias mitigation in high-stakes decision contexts.

title: AI adoption from the lens of strategic narratives and ontological security: A conceptual exploration
affiliations: Aalborg University, Aalborg University and Aalborg University

detail.title: AI adoption from the lens of strategic narratives and ontological security: A conceptual exploration
detail.abstract: As organisations strive to integrate Artificial Intelligence (AI) within their workflows through technical transformations, disruptions affect their human and cultural environments. These disruptions often threaten an organisation’s ontological security – the collective sense of identity, agency, and continuity, causing existential anxieties, resistance, and scepticism among employees. In such contexts, strategic narratives emerged as powerful tools to establish meaning-making, supporting organisations in framing technological transitions in ways that preserve identity and enhance acceptance. Although prior literature explores the role of strategic narratives in fostering technology adoption in organisations, scant research examines how these narratives interact with ontological security in the context of AI adoption. This gap is addressed by conceptually exploring the roles of strategic narratives and ontological security in AI adoption within organisations, using Rogers’ Diffusion of Innovations (DOI) theory as a foundational lens. Using a systematic literature review and inductive content analysis, this study explores the identity-based and narrative contextualization of AI within organisational change. We introduce a conceptual framework to illustrate how strategic narratives and ontological security are embedded in innovation-diffusion processes and how these processes impact organisational responses to AI adoption. This research helps redefine AI adoption beyond technical issues, highlighting the psychological and human aspects of change, particularly the importance of narratives in mitigating anxieties and resistance. In doing so, this study expands theoretical discussions of ontological security and strategic narratives into interdisciplinary areas involving organisational change, unfurling stakeholder-centric disruptions linked to technological change.

detail.abstract: This working paper argues that the use of bribery and corruption has historically been a well-established multinational strategy. It examines multiple cases of grand corruption by blue chip corporations in different time periods and geographies, although there is no means of confirming whether these prominent case studies were tips of an iceberg or outliers. The level of engagement in petty corruption cannot be established. The industrial distribution of multinational corruption has been especially skewed towards armaments and commodities. Its use was particularly prevalent in Africa, where it was frequently condoned by the home governments of the multinationals involved. Grand corruption was especially prominent when business involved large contracts with governments. Bribery was fueled by the pervasiveness of corruption in the host economies in which the multinationals operated, but the multinationals were active agents in facilitating further corruption. Although bribery and corruption are often associated in the public mind with rogue individuals, it has historically been more often the product of miscreant corporate cultures. The corruption that was extensive in Nigeria, Equatorial Guinea and elsewhere did not originate with multinationals, but the actions of some large corporations confirmed rather than countered it, putting large sums of money into the system, and providing means for corrupt profits to be recycled elsewhere. This happened in the context of weak and poorly enforced international regulation. Bribery and corruption might have reduced transaction costs in specific circumstances, but the use of corruption by multinationals in countries with fragile institutional structures, especially in Africa, was totally unproductive.

detail.abstract: Wage information is rare in job adverts, yet crucial for search. To study this information friction, we run a field experiment with real vacancies, randomly adding or withholding wage information. Disclosing wages does not change average application volumes. Instead, it amplifies the wage elasticity of applications: higher-wage vacancies receive more applicants, while lower-wage vacancies receive fewer. Average applicant quality remains unchanged, challenging standard directed search models. We rationalize the lack of skill-based sorting with two-sided limited information about applicants skills. We further show that firms decision not to post wages can act as insurance against unproductive matches.

detail.abstract: This study examines how organizations respond to performance shortfalls under escalating stretch goals, moving beyond traditional “failure = search” models to emphasize the interpretive role of cognitive framing. Drawing on the behavioral theory of the firm and managerial cognition perspectives, we employ a mixed-method design that integrates a controlled simulation experiment (Study 1) with in-depth executive interviews (Study 2). Study 1 provides causal evidence that defensive frames channel resources toward exploitative innovation, while growth-oriented frames foster exploratory reallocation, demonstrating that identical shortfalls can produce divergent outcomes depending on interpretation. Study 2 extends these insights by showing that frames are socially embedded in organizational structures, cultures, and histories, and that they can persist through reinforcing cycles or shift following shocks and managerial interventions. Together, our findings extend behavioral strategy by positioning framing as a dynamic, context-dependent mediator of performance feedback, and by identifying conditions under which stretch goals foster rigidity or renewal.

title: Heritage of Hostility: How Anti-Missionary Violence and Industrial Capacity Shaped China's Quid Pro Quo for Foreign Technology

detail.title: Heritage of Hostility: How Anti-Missionary Violence and Industrial Capacity Shaped China's Quid Pro Quo for Foreign Technology
detail.abstract: Why do some regions fail to adopt the best available technologies? This paper examines how anti-foreign sentiment, proxied by the incidence of anti-missionary violence, and industrial capacity jointly shaped the gains from China's 1983 Quid Pro Quo policy (QPQ, trading market access for technology). Our difference-indifferences analysis shows that the QPQ policy substantially increased foreign technology adoption in cities with more developed early industrial capacity. A subsequent triple-differences specification shows that anti-missionary violence erased around three-quarters of these gains, with the most pronounced effects on critical equipment, licensing agreements, and in cities where officials led the conflicts. Disaggregated analysis with stringent fixed effects demonstrates that hostility toward specific source countries sharply cut technology inflows from those countries. Mechanism analysis suggests that anti-missionary violence contributed to this erosion by deteriorating bilateral municipal ties and deterring the entry of foreign-invested firms. Firm-level matching indicates a 15.8% productivity premium for technology adopters, and a back-of-the-envelope calculation translates this into an average city-level productivity shortfall of 0.128% over 1983-1995 due to antiforeign sentiment.

detail.abstract: This study presents the Syntactic Authority Index (SAI) as a quantitative measure of linguistic authority within financial discourse and evaluates its predictive capacity for market behavior. By detecting recurrent authority-bearing constructions such as deontic modalities, nominalizations, enumerations, and passive imperatives, the index demonstrates how linguistic form itself carries institutional weight. The regla compilada, understood as a Type-0 production that binds constraints to model decisions, functions as the generative substrate connecting syntax to observable financial reactions. Using multilingual corpora of earnings calls, investor letters, and regulatory filings, the research examines whether variations in the SAI precede abnormal returns, volume shifts, and regulatory enforcement events. Out-of-sample evaluations show that increases in syntactic authority correlate with short-term market anomalies while remaining independent of sentiment or tone. The signal intensifies under macroeconomic uncertainty or within firms under regulatory observation. These findings indicate that linguistic form operates as an actionable signal, showing that authority encoded in syntax can coordinate expectations and influence market conduct without relying on authorial intent.

title: Skill-Biased Technical Change and the Decline of Thailand's Skill Premium
affiliations: The University of Western Australia

detail.title: Skill-Biased Technical Change and the Decline of Thailand's Skill Premium
detail.abstract: This paper examines the long-term dynamics of the skill premium in Thailand, focusing on the roles of skill-biased technical change (SBTC), product demand shifts and changes in skill supply. Like many developing countries, Thailand exhibits an inverted Ushaped pattern, with rising inequality until the late 2000s and convergence thereafter. Using the race between education and technology (RBET) framework, the analysis highlights the dominant role of technical bias in driving these dynamics. While technology significantly contributed to rising inequality in the late 1990s and early 2000s, its influence has since diminished. Although the country's production structure has shifted toward lowskilled sectors, reducing demand for skilled labor, this effect is secondary to that of technology. The findings suggest that the current convergence in wages is not a sign of balanced labor market. To reverse this trend, policymakers should prioritize investments in high-tech industries and advanced technologies to stimulate demand for skilled labor.

title: Ambidextrous Competence in the Void: The Asymmetric Deployment of Leadership Styles in High Power-Distance Emerging Markets

detail.title: Ambidextrous Competence in the Void: The Asymmetric Deployment of Leadership Styles in High Power-Distance Emerging Markets

keywords.keywords: Leadership CompetencyInstitutional VoidContextual AmbidexterityEndogeneity MitigationHigh Power-Distance (HPD)Transactional Leadership

detail.abstract: This study challenges the assumed universality of Western leadership models by examining the dual-pathway mechanism through which Leadership Competency (LC) is translated into performance within high power-distance (HPD) and institutionally void emerging markets. Drawing primarily on Institutional Theory and the Resource-Based View (RBV), we introduce the Dynamic Leadership Synthesis (DLS) framework, positing that LC acts as a VRIN institutional substitute whose effectiveness relies on its contextually ambidextrous deployment. Analyzing three-wave, multi-source data from 581 leader–subordinate dyads in Ethiopian banks, we employ a Structural Equation Model with Lags (T1, T2, T3) to mitigate endogeneity and test a novel moderated-mediation mechanism. Results confirm an asymmetric deployment logic: LC improves performance (BP) indirectly via two distinct pathways—Employee Engagement (EE) and Organizational Culture (OC). Crucially, the structural (OC) pathway demonstrates superior potency (2.2× the EE effect), underscoring a structural primacy logic. We find that Transformational Leadership (TL) selectively amplifies the motivational (EE) pathway, while Transactional Leadership (TxL) reinforces the structural (OC) pathway. These findings compel a decolonial rebalancing of leadership theory, repositioning leadership styles as contingent stabilizers and mobilizers essential for navigating the competing demands of structural hierarchy and institutional uncertainty.

detail.abstract: This paper examines how the United States has repeatedly monetized failure, from the neglect of Vietnam veterans to the expansion of mass incarceration after Terry v. Ohio (1968). Whereas the U.S. justice system and welfare bureaucracy have historically generated profit through punishment, auditing, and exclusion, alternative models from Finland and Canada demonstrate the viability of redirecting investment into human restoration. The proposed framework, treating human productivity as a stock-backed asset, offers a hybrid between welfare and capitalism. Veterans, the disabled, and structurally displaced workers would not be burdens but beneficiaries, generating measurable returns in reduced homelessness, lower incarceration costs, and higher productivity. America, long considered the "largest welfare state in the world," but lacking transparency, could reorient its capital from punishment industries into dignity industries.

publicationDetails.journalName: IZA Institute of Labor Economics Discussion Paper Series

detail.abstract: Women remain underrepresented in leadership worldwide. Across politics, business, and community organizations, they face barriers limiting access to leadership roles and influence in decision-making. This paper groups these barriers into opportunity, motivation, and capability, and reviews global evidence on interventions to address them. It assesses the effectiveness of these approaches, how descriptive representation (holding a leadership position) translates into substantive representation (influencing decisions), and unintended consequences. Quotas can increase women's descriptive representation when well designed and enforced. Role model interventions may motivate participation, mainly in politics, though evidence is mixed elsewhere. Training, mentorship, and organizational reforms show context specific results, often supporting career progression rather than leadership attainment. Greater numerical representation does not always yield substantive influence. Outcomes depend on institutional context, gender norms, and complementary support. Advancing women's leadership requires strategies that address multiple barriers and further research on how representation translates into real influence.

detail.abstract: We analyze the impact of AI-augmented training on worker productivity in a financial services company. The company introduced an AI tool that provides performance feedback on call center agents to guide their training. To estimate causal effects, we exploit the staggered roll out of the AI-tool. The AI-augmented training reduces call handling time by 10 percent. We find larger effects for short-tenured workers because they spend less time putting clients on hold. But the AI-augmented training also improves communication style with relatively stronger effects for long-tenured agents, and we find slightly positive effects on customer satisfaction.

detail.abstract: The study evaluates the effect of corporate social responsibility (CSR) on business performance moderated by governance factors, specifically non-executive directors (NEDs), using data from Vietnamese commercial banks from 2014 to 2024. The analysis employs models FGLS (Feasible Generalized Least Squares) and an unbalanced panel dataset comprising 20 commercial banks. NEDs are crucial in improving banks' business performance in the framework of sustainable development, according to the research findings, which also indicate that CSR has a detrimental effect on business performance in all three models of ROA, ROE, and NIM. While bad debt has a negative effect on performance indicators, the study also discovered that internal factors like Bank Size and LDR ratio have a positive relationship with business performance. Bank asset efficiency is negatively impacted by Inflation, while bank performance is positively impacted by Population growth and Foreign direct investment. The foundation for suggesting practical management implications for corporate operations in the framework of sustainable development is the synthesis of research findings.

detail.abstract: The present chapter elaborates on the legal theory or jurisprudential foundations informing the notion of European transnational private law. Building upon the influential scholarship by Anu Bradford and Joanne Scott on the global reach of EU law, the chapter traces the widespread reliance in contemporary legal thought on proceduralisation parameters as a benchmark to foster regulatory quality and integrity with the relatively overlooked articulation of process-based legal theories during the 1950s. Through an interconnected reading of the seminal works of Hart and Sacks, McDougal and Lasswell, and Jessup, the chapter shows how-despite their different focuses and outlooks-these postwar authors offer a coherent, innovative, and appealing conception of law that encompasses the national, international, and transnational contexts, and that largely transcends the contemporary appeals to proceduralisation as a mere simile to standards of due process or natural justice. The chapter signifies this conception as the 'jurisprudence of process'. After highlighting its relationship with the developments of European law and legal thought, the chapter deploys the jurisprudence of process as a framework to renovate contemporary studies on the global reach of EU law based on conceptual, analytical, and theoretical grounds. In this way, the chapter elaborates a renewed jurisprudential baseline for the prospective engagement with European transnational private law as a scholarly research agenda and as a matter of practical lawyering.

title: Data-Driven Bed Occupancy Planning in Intensive Care Units Using Mt/Gt/∞ Queueing Models

detail.title: Data-Driven Bed Occupancy Planning in Intensive Care Units Using Mt/Gt/∞ Queueing Models
detail.abstract: Hospitals struggle to make effective long-term capacity planning decisions for intensive care units (ICUs) under uncertainty in future demand. Admission rates fluctuate over time due to temporal factors, and length of stay (LOS) distributions vary with patient heterogeneity, hospital location, case mix, and clinical practices. Common planning approaches rely on steady-state queueing models or heuristic rules that assume fixed parameters, but these methods often fall short in capturing real-world occupancy dynamics. One widely used example is the 85% occupancy rule, which recommends maintaining average utilization below this level to ensure responsiveness; however, this rule is based on stationary assumptions and may be unreliable when applied to time-varying systems. Our analysis shows that even when long-run utilization targets are met, day-to-day occupancy frequently exceeds 100% capacity.We propose a data-driven framework for estimating ICU bed occupancy using an Mt/Gt/∞ queueing model, which incorporates time-varying arrival rates and empirically estimated LOS distributions. The framework combines statistical decomposition and parametric distribution fitting to capture temporal patterns in ICU admissions and LOS. We apply it to multi-year data from neonatal ICUs (NICUs) in Calgary as a case study. Several capacity planning scenarios are evaluated, including average-based thresholds and surge estimates from Poisson overflow approximations. Results demonstrate the inadequacy of static heuristics in environments with fluctuating demand and highlight the importance of modeling LOS variability when estimating bed needs. Although the case study focuses on NICUs, the methodology generalizes to other ICU settings and provides interpretable, data-informed support for healthcare systems facing rising demand and limited capacity.

title: Managerial Criminal Adversarialism

detail.title: Managerial Criminal Adversarialism

publicationDetails.detailsText: Accepted for publication in the Ohio State Journal on Dispute Resolution (OSU JDR), Volume 42, Fall 2026.

detail.abstract:
The rise of managerial judging in criminal procedure over the past two decades has fundamentally transformed the adversarial model of adjudication, reshaping the judge’s role from a neutral arbiter into an active case manager. Under this model, courts now proactively facilitate, endorse, encourage, and mediate guilty pleas in pursuit of efficiency. While managerial imperatives have begun to take root in several U.S. states, this article highlights a critical concern that judicial regulation has yet to address – the bureaucratization of the criminal process. 

Scholars have long raised concerns about judicial involvement in plea bargaining and the demise of the adversarial trial. However, this article argues that managerialism does not necessarily erode the adversarial framework. By grounding managerial-led guilty pleas on the adversarial principles of liberty and consent, it merely exacerbates longstanding risks within plea-bargaining, such as wrongful convictions, coercion, pressures to plead, and prosecutorial dominance – all contributing to the current mass discriminatory incarceration system. While scholars have offered to utilize managerial tools and judicial regulation to mitigate prosecutorial dominance and ensure evidentiary sufficiency, the article argues that the broader shift toward bureaucratic case management, with efficiency as an overarching objective, displaces the adversarial ideal of autonomy and meaningful participation. The rise of virtual guilty pleas further amplifies this problem by severing defendants from the courtroom process and detaching plea decisions from the trial’s retributive function. 

Given that the criminal trial serves not merely as a mechanism for case disposal but as a process that holds defendants to account, guilty pleas must be genuine, sincere, and voluntary, not mere products of a bureaucratic system. Ultimately, while managerialism preserves the adversarial process in form, its bureaucratic nature transforms the trial from a forum for accountability into an administrative mechanism designed for swift convictions.

detail.abstract: Children have the potential to drive the adoption of alternative proteins (AP), yet limited studies explore children's perceptions, alongside their parents', using developed frameworks such as the Capability, Opportunity and Motivations of model of Behaviour (COM-B). Through an online questionnaire, we aimed to understand children and parents' awareness and consumption of plant-based meat, cultivated meat and insect proteins in Singapore and their willingness to try (WTT) and willingness to regularly consume (WTC). We also examined which COMB domains predicted WTT and WTC as well as factors that predicted parent's willingness to let their child try (LCT) and willingness to let their child regularly consume (LCC). Children (N=266; M=11.47-years-old) and parents (N=269; M=42.34-years-old) were most familiar with and reported greatest previous consumption of plant-based meats, compared to the other AP types. Among children, motivation was a significant predictor of WTT (ps≤.015), and capability was a significant predictor of WTC (ps≤.019) for all AP. For parents, motivation was a significant predictor of WTT and WTC for all types (except WTT plant based and WTC cultivated meat; ps≤.003) and capability significantly predicted WTC cultivated meat and plantbased meat (ps ≤.030). Opportunity was not a significant predictor for either WTT or WTC for children and parents. AP adding value to the child's diet were significant predictors of LCT and LCC (ps≤.004). Our results help to uncover the complex nature of consumer perceptions of AP, and we make recommendation of interventions that could be developed.

detail.abstract: The UPPS-P model of impulsivity includes five impulsigenic traits: positive urgency, negative urgency, lack of premeditation, lack of perseverance, and sensation seeking. The present study employed experience sampling methodology to examine the associations of impulsigenic traits with daily-life experiences including affect, social functioning, situation appraisals, and substance use (n=601). Positive urgency, negative urgency, lack of premeditation, and lack of perseverance were associated with emotional dysfunction, disorganized experiences, and communication disruptions, whereas sensation seeking was associated with elevated positive affect and diminished negative affect. detail.abstract: Car-following (CF) models serve as the core framework for microscopic traffic simulation and for controlling longitudinal motion in adaptive and cooperative adaptive cruise control (ACC and CACC) systems. While several comprehensive studies have aimed to identify gaps in existing models, many have focused on a limited range of models or have not established a framework to synthesize and compare their performance across key dimensions. To fill this gap, this review analyzes 251 records, focusing on four theory-driven models and three intelligent families. Evaluation is structured around safety, comfort, calibration, explainability, mixed-traffic realism, emissions and energy, and human factors. No single model family performs best across all criteria. Theory-driven models, due to their simpler formulations, are more interpretable and easier to integrate into simulation platforms but are highly sensitive to calibration and struggle under heterogeneous or adverse conditions. Fuzzy systems maintain interpretability yet lack formal safety verification and standardized calibration, which limits their generalization. Data-driven models improve predictive accuracy and reduce oscillations but face challenges in generalization, safety assurance, and emissions modeling. Emerging hybrid approaches, such as physics-informed learning, offer a promising balance between predictive accuracy and control-relevant guarantees. Reinforcement learning (RL) has also emerged as a promising paradigm by enabling multi-objective optimization through reward shaping. Furthermore, a two-stage pipeline is outlined, coupling supervised predictive baselines with reinforcement learning-based multi-objective refinement to embed empirical realism alongside explicit safety, comfort, and emissions objectives. This review addresses current gaps and outlines recent advancements and future directions in car-following model research.

title: Adjusting for Intercurrent Events using Bayesian Joint Models for Longitudinal Outcomes in Clinical Trials
affiliations: University of Toronto - Lunenfeld-Tanenbaum Research Institute, University of Ottawa - Ottawa Hospital Research Institute, affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of Toronto - University Health Network, University of Toronto - University Health Network and University of Toronto - The Hospital for Sick Children - SickKids

detail.title: Adjusting for Intercurrent Events using Bayesian Joint Models for Longitudinal Outcomes in Clinical Trials
detail.abstract: Background:  Intercurrent events in clinical trials can disrupt the interpretation and/or measurement of clinical endpoints. While the composite variable strategy is recommended for such events that prevent outcome measurement, it is not always suitable, particularly for physical signs. This highlights the need for a novel methodology to effectively handle these intercurrent events. Methods:  We propose a Bayesian joint modeling approach to account for terminal intercurrent events. Our model jointly analyzes longitudinal outcomes and these events using shared random effects. We employ multiple discrete-time survival submodels to handle various event types and evaluate the method's type I error and power through extensive simulations that mirror a clinical trial with recovery and death as competing events. Results:  The proposed Bayesian joint modeling strategy demonstrates higher statistical power compared to models that do not consider intercurrent events. Specifically, our approach shows an increase in power of approximately 15% when bias from intercurrent events is significant and can be mitigated by joint modeling. Conclusion:  Our Bayesian joint modeling approach effectively addresses terminal intercurrent events in both the design and analysis phases of clinical trials. This method serves as an extension of the composite variable strategy for events that cannot be directly incorporated into the outcome definition.

detail.title: Welfare Effects of Market Research
detail.abstract: I study how an upstream market research firm provides information about demand conditions to a downstream product market. Demand can be high or low. The market research firm provides private signals to atomistic firms that compete with each other by producing quantities of an undifferentiated product. The market research firm chooses its information to maximize the fee it collects. I solve for equilibria of this game and demonstrate that the market research firm chooses an equilibrium to maximize the joint producer surplus. In environments where uncertainty about demand is small and strategic externalities between producers are weak, full information maximizes consumer, producer, and total surplus. In other environments, consumer, producer, and total surplus are not necessarily aligned.

detail.title: Launch support: Managing Complementor Bottlenecks in the Disruptive Innovation of Small Satellites
detail.abstract: Through both qualitative and quantitative analyses of large-rocket providers' support for small-satellite manufacturers before the emergence of small rockets, we examine how disruptors to an incumbent ecosystem gain support from complementors of the incumbent technology. Our analyses illuminate the incumbent complementors' adjustment costs arising from cospecialization with specific incumbent technology designs and resource dependency on major incumbent technology customers. These adjustment costs dis-incentivize incumbent complementors from supporting the disruptors. In addition, we demonstrate that strategies adopted by the disruptors, such as technological standardization and forward integration, help mitigate these adjustment costs and incentivize incumbent complementors to support the disruptive innovation.

detail.title: The United Kingdom Debate over the Tobacco and Vapes Bill 2024-25 (UK)
detail.abstract: This report provides a detailed analysis of the landmark Tobacco and Vapes Bill 2024-25 (UK). This pioneering public health legislation introduced by the government of Keir Starmer provides for smokefree generations and smokefree spaces in the United Kingdom. This report provides a comprehensive survey of the debate over the Tobacco and Vapes Bill 2024-25 (UK) in the United Kingdom Parliament, and the broader community. It considers the political discussion of the bill in the House of Commons and the House of Lords, as the House of Lords Committee engages in a line by line review of the bill. This report considers the political positions of the main parties in the United Kingdom Parliament-considering the stances of the Labour Party (UK), the Conservative Opposition, the Liberal Democrats, and Reform UK. This report considers the impact of the tobacco endgame policy on public health in the United Kingdom. As a case study, this study explores the impact of the tobacco control legislation in regional areas, such as Cheshire and Merseyside. Given that this legislation seeks to enact United Kingdom standards, this study also examines the support for bill in Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland. This report also charts comparative developments in New Zealand and Australia in terms of public health measures in respect of tobacco control and e-cigarette regulation. It is noted that the Tobacco and Vapes Bill 2024-25 (UK) is justified and proportionate under the European Convention on Human Rights. The Tobacco and Vapes Bill 2024-25 (UK) is also discussed in light of international law-including international environmental law; international trade and investment law; and international health law. The tobacco endgame regime of the Tobacco and Vapes Bill 2024-25 (UK) represents a powerful and compelling implementation of the WHO Framework Convention on Tobacco Control 2003.

detail.abstract: This scientific article is dedicated to the peculiarities of legal differentiation in the border sphere in Ukraine. The article examines legislative and regulatory acts that have regulated the functioning of the border service during different periods of its existence. It also analyzes the process of its formation and development as an important component of Ukraine’s national and state security system. The article discusses its role in ensuring the protection of Ukraine’s state border. Additionally, an analysis of international experience in the field of protecting state borders of European countries has been conducted, which demonstrates the need for clearly defined priorities and appropriate strategies for the development of mechanisms for the protection and defense of shared state borders. The obtained results allowed us to establish that in the majority of European Union (EU) countries, the functions of border control are carried out by law enforcement agencies within the police force. In some countries, such as Malta (and partially in Spain), the control of maritime borders is entrusted to the armed forces. Several EU countries have specialized bodies or agencies (border services) that specifically deal with border-related issues outside the competence of the police. This applies to Finland, Latvia, Lithuania, the Netherlands, Poland, and Switzerland, where border guards have law enforcement powers in certain cases. Additionally, the national services responsible for external border control are often subordinate to various ministries, most of which are ministries of internal affairs, while in other countries, they also include the Ministry of Defense (France, Italy, Norway, Portugal, Spain, Sweden, and the Netherlands). International experience in safeguarding national borders in European countries emphasizes the importance of establishing clear priorities and development strategies for border protection and defense mechanisms. Over a significant period of time, international cooperation in this field has been evolving and actively implemented. Alongside the governing bodies of the European Union, key participants in this process are the border agencies of EU member states that share common borders. They operate based on bilateral and multilateral agreements on cooperation and mutual assistance in border-related matters, as well as international documents pertaining to border security. The article draws conclusions about positive changes in the legal status of the State Border Guard Service of Ukraine that have taken place over the past decade and examines the problems of legal differentiation in the border sphere in Ukraine due to russian aggression. In particular, due to fundamental differences between functions and tasks performed by the State Border Guard Service of Ukraine along different sections of Ukraine’s state border, as well as in connection with russian aggression, the idea of legal differentiation in the border sphere has been proposed. This would involve the creation of a separate military formation called the «Border Defense Forces» in the east and south of Ukraine, which would be integrated into the Armed Forces of Ukraine. In the western part of the country, the State Border Guard Service of Ukraine would remain under the Ministry of Internal Affairs of Ukraine, taking into account global experience in the protection, defense, and security of state borders by other countries.

detail.title: Business Sentiment and FDI Dynamics in China: An Econometric Assessment of Investor Confidence
detail.abstract: 1. AbstractIn the current landscape of China's economic malaise and rising geopolitical tensions, the media presents a situation of capital flight, while the actual situation for foreign investment in China is more nuanced. While FDI literature has long emphasized macroeconomic drivers, less is known about how localized investor sentiment predicts FDI movement. We examine the relationship between business sentiment and foreign direct investment (FDI) in China using survey data from major international chambers of commerce in China and macroeconomic indicators from 2007 to 2025. Responses on business performance, outlook, and investment preference were standardized into a five-point Likert scale to construct an integrated sentiment index. Trend, correlation, and regression analyses were applied to assess the relationship between member responses of investor sentiment and FDI. The results reveal statistically significant downward trends in business performance and outlook, while investment preference remains largely flat, indicating persistent long-term commitment amid weaker short-term confidence. Correlation and feature-importance testing show that labor costs, GDP growth, and business outlook exert the strongest influence on FDI intensity, explaining a substantial portion of observed variation. Compared with the global Kearney FDI Confidence Index (FDIC), the locally derived index demonstrates closer alignment with realized investment behavior, capturing firm-level dynamics more accurately. These findings suggest that domestic business sentiment can serve as an early indicator of FDI movement and provide policymakers with a practical framework for monitoring investor confidence, identifying emerging risks, and designing targeted measures to improve their position for investors.

declarations.funderStatement: Cross-Border Data Forum, Ford Foundation, Georgia Tech School of Cybersecurity and Privacy, Microsoft, and the Yale Law School Paul Tsai China Center.

detail.abstract:
In the recent past, notably since the beginning of 2024, national security has been used as the rationale for multiple significant U.S. legal measures, to limit the transfer of data about individuals to so-called “countries of concern,” especially including China. These measures include the Protecting Americans’ Data from Foreign Adversaries Act and the Department of Justice Bulk Data Rule. This article is the first to consider these legal measures as a unified topic – in each of them, personal data is being treated for the first time in U.S. law as a “dual-use” technology, with both military and civilian applications. 

Part II of this Article introduces the U.S. export control regime to privacy experts and others who have previously had little reason to consider export controls. From the standpoint of the U.S.-China relations field, Part III highlights additional new laws that treat data as a dual-use technology. Part IV explains how three major regions – the European Union, China, and the U.S. – have taken distinct legal approaches to treating personal data as a dual-use technology, although recently China and U.S. have shown convergence in their approaches. 

Part V presents the privacy case for dual-use regulation of personal data. The relationship between privacy and national security has historically been what we call “Privacy OR National Security.” With limits on exporting data, we may instead see “Privacy AND National Security,” with privacy advocates supporting export rules to limit the practices of data brokers and the online advertising industry. 

Part VI presents important reasons from the International Relations literature for caution about the advisability of dual-use regulation of personal data. 

Drawing on these multiple perspectives, Part VII critically assesses the recent surge in dual-use regulation of personal data. The prima facie case supporting such regulations appears strong. With that said, the Article presents the case for serious second thoughts about expanding such dual-use measures, and concludes with normative recommendations.

detail.title: Employer-Employee Matching and Complementary Assets: The Role of Cross-Organization Collaborations. [On-line Appendices]
detail.abstract:
Building on human capital theory and social capital theory, we theorize that cross-organization collaborations generate a rich and distinct source of relational capital that enhances employer-employee matches when complementary assets are important in the production process. We test our theory in the context of academic scientists where collaborations within and across organizations are common ways to access complementary assets. We find that cross-organizational collaborations are positively related to an individual’s decision to move towards their previous co-authors. Additionally, moving to an organization where an individual had a direct collaboration is positively related to post-mobility performance. This suggests that prior collaboration facilitates better employer-employee matches. We unpack this finding and show that the post-mobility performance increase is not driven only by increased productivity with the prior co-authors, it is also driven by novel collaborations with new colleagues. Together, our findings suggest that cross-organization collaborations facilitate hiring employees that can integrate well with the complementary assets of the entire unit. 


Full paper available at: 

Campbell, B. A., Di Lorenzo, F., & Tartari, V. (2021). Employer–employee matching and complementary assets: The role of cross-organization collaborations. Academy of Management Journal, 64(3), 799-823. https://doi.org/10.5465/amj.2019.0207

detail.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is transforming marketing practice by enhancing personalization, automation, and decision-making. Yet, many organizations struggle to connect tactical AI applications with long-term strategic goals. This paper introduces the Business Chessboard Strategy (BCS), a conceptual framework that maps key organizational components-vision, strategy, processes, culture, innovation, and operations-onto chess pieces. Drawing on a mixed-methods study of 120 marketing professionals and 15 expert interviews, the research identifies strategic imbalances between tactical efficiency and cultural or visionary readiness. The BCS framework provides an integrative and visual tool to help managers align short-term AI initiatives with overarching strategic intent. By bridging theory and practice, BCS contributes to interactive marketing research by translating complex AI-driven dynamics into actionable strategic insights.

detail.abstract: Macroprudential policies are a key policy tool for financial regulators, but concerns persist that these policies restrict access to homeownership. I examine this concern using crosscountry data on homeownership for 28 countries. I find little evidence that macroprudential policies reduce homeownership rates in aggregate or for select groups such as low-income households. The estimates are precise enough to rule out large negative effects of macroprudential policies on homeownership rates. The null effects are consistent with models where credit shocks primarily affect prices rather than quantities. My results alleviate concerns that macroprudential policies systematically exclude certain households from ownership, but also indicate that relaxing such policies is unlikely to increase access to homeownership.
